newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - DEC 5.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - DEC 5.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- The ruling Socialist party and the government are likely to decide today who will be the new Welfare Minister.

- The parliament committee investigating the case of irregular payments to a state privatisation agency (APV) consultant, Marta Tocsik, tries to clarify today if confidential information leaked from the committee.
- The police considers providing Marta Tocsik and her barrister, who have been threatened with killing, with guards.
- Private companies sue the Justice Ministry saying the ministry breached the competition law by selling information.
- The Parliament's Agricultural Committee backs the proposal which would allow the government to spend more on agricultural subsidies next year than originally planned.
- The police have prepared a drawing about the man suspected with exploding a bomb on Wednesday, and offered a reward of one million forints for the person who help them find the bomber.
